name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
principle: The product deserializes attacker-controlled bytes without ensuring the reconstructed object is valid and expected. Deserialization can instantiate unsafe types, invoke gadget methods, alter object state, or consume excessive resources before normal validation runs.
detection_signals: Java ObjectInputStream.readObject() on FileInputStream, ServletInputStream, Socket.getInputStream(), request body, or uploaded file
Java readObject(), readResolve(), finalize(), or Comparator gadget class reachable from deserialized input
Java Jackson enableDefaultTyping()/activateDefaultTyping() or polymorphic @JsonTypeInfo on untrusted JSON
Java org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml.load() on untrusted YAML without SafeConstructor
C++ boost::archive::*_iarchive >> object from socket/file/request without prior authentication and type allowlist
C/C++ custom unserialize/read/recv parser allocates objects or dispatches function pointers/vtables from encoded type names or IDs
negative_signals: Java ObjectInputFilter setObjectInputFilter() or global jdk.serialFilter restricts maxdepth, maxbytes, and allowed classes before readObject()
HMAC/signature verification over the exact serialized bytes occurs before any deserialization call
Deserialization replaced by parsing into fixed DTO/value types with schema validation and no polymorphic type metadata
Class defines private/final readObject(ObjectInputStream) that always throws IOException to forbid deserialization
Apache Commons IO ValidatingObjectInputStream.accept() or equivalent allowlist is configured before readObject()
Sensitive or environment-derived Java fields are declared transient and reinitialized after validation
false_defense_traps: Base64-decoding input before readObject() is not validation
Checking authentication or HMAC after readObject() is too late
Class-name blacklist blocks only known gadgets and misses new gadget chains
Client-side encryption/signing is bypassable if the client or key is compromised
WAF filtering does not cover all serialized input formats or alternate input paths
verification_focus: Can attacker-controlled bytes reach a deserialization API before integrity verification, type allowlisting, and object/state validation are enforced?

consequence_chains.trigger: serialized data controls object fields or dynamically determined attributes
consequence_chains.consequence: integrity loss through unexpected state or unauthorized data modification

consequence_chains.trigger: serialized stream encodes very large, cyclic, or deeply nested object graphs
consequence_chains.consequence: CPU or memory denial of service

consequence_chains.trigger: available gadget chain executes code during readObject/readResolve/constructor callbacks
consequence_chains.consequence: remote code execution or shell command execution

patch_principle: Do not deserialize untrusted data; use simple formats and populate new validated DTOs instead.
Authenticate serialized bytes with HMAC/signature before deserialization.
Enforce strict class allowlists and resource limits before the first deserialization call.
Disable or reject deserialization for classes that do not need it with a throwing readObject().
Remove unnecessary gadget-capable libraries and mark sensitive fields transient.

minimal_examples.safe: if (!validHmac(bytes)) throw new SecurityException(); ObjectInputFilter.Config.setObjectInputFilter(in, allowlistFilter); MyDto obj = (MyDto) in.readObject();
